One of the greatest Spider-Man opening sequences ever put on screen. @hanszimmer Cooked Here. 

Hans Zimmer alongside his supergroup collective The Magnificent Six didn’t just score the opening sequence of The Amazing Spider-Man 2, he turned Andrew Garfield’s free-fall into pure cinematic euphoria. The soaring brass, energetic percussion, and sheer scale of the track "I'm Spider-Man" give every web-slinging turn through the Manhattan skyline an undeniable adrenaline rush. Paired with Marc Webb's dynamic camera work as Peter chases down the stolen plutonium truck, it remains one of the most visually stunning swinging sequences in comic book movie history.

What makes this sequence hit so hard isn't just the sheer scale of the CGI; it’s the effortless joy and swagger Andrew Garfield brings to the suit. Over a decade later, no modern blockbuster has managed to capture the physical speed and momentum of a hero in flight quite like this. It’s a masterclass in how a world-class score can transform a high-stakes action beat into pure, unadulterated spectacle.
